svg.text: A C string ends at the first '\0' byte, not at the end of its array
Label printer, customer "Nguyen Thi Phuong Thao" (22 chars + '\0' = 23 bytes). Blue cell = '\0', red = written past name, ? = never written.
strcpy(name, customer): 23 bytes into a 16-byte array
Undefined behaviour. On this -O0 build the 7 extra bytes land in city, so the label prints CITY: g Thao
strncpy(name, customer, 16): exactly 16 bytes copied, no '\0' added
name is not a string any more: printf("%s", name) reads on until a '\0' (UB) and prints Nguyen Thi PhuonBinh Duong
printf starts at name[0] and stops at the first '\0' it finds: city[10], 26 bytes later (strncpy padded city with '\0')
snprintf(name, sizeof name, "%s", customer) returns 22, and 22 >= 16 means it was cut
At most 15 chars + '\0' are written, never past name[15]; city keeps "Binh Duong" and the caller can warn about the cut
